Business.description: What the major business and general-news outlets are leading with.
Business.overview: Business outlets are dominated by a sudden bout of AI-bubble anxiety after Alphabet's disappointing cash burn and Google's capex spike rattled the Nasdaq, compounding worries over AI-related corporate debt. That overlaps with major central-bank news (the Fed holding rates steady under Chair Kevin Warsh and Christine Lagarde's surprise early ECB exit), a wave of mixed Q3 earnings, and the UK's post-Budget economic fallout.

stories.headline: Alphabet's AI spending spree spooks investors despite strong revenue
stories.summary: Google shares fell sharply after Alphabet's third-quarter results showed a widening cash burn tied to a $51 billion AI infrastructure bill, with search growth also slowing more than expected as AI changes query behavior.

stories.headline: Federal Reserve holds rates steady, Warsh resists signaling December move
stories.summary: The Fed left its benchmark rate unchanged at 3.75%-4% despite elevated inflation, with two officials dissenting in favor of a hike and Chair Kevin Warsh declining to give forward guidance on whether rates will rise again in December.

stories.headline: Christine Lagarde to resign early as ECB president
stories.summary: Lagarde will step down in February, months before her eight-year term was due to end, triggering a selection process among European leaders just as debt problems and inflation resurface.

stories.headline: Hong Kong leader apologizes over deadly Tai Po apartment fire
stories.summary: Chief Executive John Lee issued a rare apology for the city's deadliest fire in decades and announced his housing secretary's resignation, while still defending the broader government response.

stories.headline: AI debt worries intensify as credit markets show strain
stories.summary: Credit default swaps are signaling rising risk around data-center bonds, adding to a broader narrative that investors may be reaching their limit on AI-linked debt just as tech earnings reveal cash-flow strain.

stories.headline: Storied law firm Weil Gotshal to shut down after partner exodus
stories.summary: Weil Gotshal is winding down and has tapped restructuring advisers to steer the process after a wave of high-profile partner departures and collapsed merger talks left it with few options.

stories.headline: Oil slips as traders weigh signs of Iran diplomacy
stories.summary: Crude prices eased as markets assessed fresh diplomatic overtures, including a letter from US Vice President JD Vance to Iranian officials, aimed at averting renewed US strikes.

stories.headline: Eli Lilly and Merck beat estimates on blockbuster drug demand
stories.summary: Eli Lilly raised its sales outlook as Zepbound and Mounjaro demand surged again, while Merck also topped estimates and lifted guidance on stronger-than-expected Keytruda sales including a new injectable form.

Business.gaps: No stories within the last 24-48 hours could be found from Puck or The Information via search; Forbes and Business Insider yielded only older AI-infrastructure analysis pieces outside the window; Axios's business/economy pages showed mostly AI-bubble commentary without a clear distinct lead story in the timeframe. BBC, WSJ, NYT, FT, The Economist and Politico were covered via their provided feed items only, since these outlets block broader web search.

US politics.overview: Coverage across outlets is overwhelmingly focused on the final stretch before the Nov. 3 midterms, with nonpartisan forecasters and reporters converging on a narrative of a building Democratic wave in the House and a toss-up Senate. A parallel thread running through legal and policy outlets is the Trump administration's unprecedented last-minute push to control state election processes, which is running into repeated court losses.

stories.headline: Forecasters see Democrats poised for a major midterm wave, Senate a true toss-up
stories.summary: With days to go, RealClearPolitics reports Democrats are on track for their largest generic-ballot advantage since 2008, a finding echoed by Cook Political Report's shift of House seats toward Democrats and Punchbowl's reporting that House Republicans privately are bracing for a 'blowout,' even as the Senate majority remains genuinely contested.

stories.headline: Judge rejects Trump administration bid to control California's vote count
stories.summary: A federal judge found the Trump administration was attempting to take over California's elections process by trying to set aside or sequester ballots over unproven noncitizen-voting claims, and the DOJ has already filed notice it will appeal.

stories.headline: Courts become the last battleground as Trump's election-control push collides with Nov. 3
stories.summary: Stateline reports that with less than a week until Election Day, a series of courtroom fights over President Trump's drive for more power over state election administration could reach resolution just before voting ends, alongside separate reporting that DOJ plans to send 1,000 election monitors to all 50 states without disclosing locations.

stories.headline: Senate battleground map expands deep into red territory: South Carolina, Florida, Mississippi
stories.summary: Senate Democrats are increasingly optimistic about a bigger-than-expected blue wave as polls show South Carolina, Florida and Mississippi all newly competitive, a dynamic RealClearPolitics separately describes as a 'train wreck' moment for the GOP in South Carolina.

stories.headline: Speaker Johnson signals he'll stay atop House GOP even if Republicans lose the majority
stories.summary: Mike Johnson's recent hints that he intends to remain the top House Republican regardless of the midterm outcome have reportedly rattled the party's internal leadership outlook just days before the election.

stories.headline: Trump's attacks on Michigan Senate candidate El-Sayed's faith dominate the race's final days
stories.summary: After President Trump labeled Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed a 'jihadist,' El-Sayed dismissed the attack as 'desperate, bad faith,' a storyline also touched on by Fox News coverage of Rep. Ilhan Omar's GOP challenger highlighting immigration and crime issues.

stories.headline: Civil rights groups sue over DHS targeting of naturalized citizens in voter investigations
stories.summary: Civil rights groups allege in a new lawsuit that the Department of Homeland Security is unlawfully scrutinizing naturalized U.S. citizens in ways that put them at risk of disenfranchisement just before the midterms, a story that comes alongside NPR's report that hackers leaked the identities of more than 40,000 DHS employees.

stories.headline: Hundreds of millions spent on state ballot measures covering billionaire taxes, abortion, trans rights and voting
stories.summary: Politico reports at least $400 million has been spent on TV ads for this cycle's state ballot initiatives, a theme NPR also covers in detailing votes on abortion bans in Missouri and a proposed billionaire wealth tax in California.

US politics.gaps: NOTUS had no items from the last 24-48 hours in search results (most recent relevant pieces were weeks to months old). NYT, WSJ, The Guardian, and the original Politico feed could only be assessed via the provided feed items since these outlets block web search.

Tech & AI.overview: Coverage is dominated by the market shockwaves from Big Tech's Q3 earnings, with Alphabet and Microsoft both posting record results but spooking investors over AI capital spending, alongside major AI product launches (Google's Gemini 4 Carbon) and Anthropic's accelerating IPO push. Security incidents, including a large government data breach and a Meta smart glasses privacy probe, also feature prominently.

stories.headline: Alphabet and Microsoft earnings spark AI spending anxiety on Wall Street
stories.summary: Google shares fell as much as 10% after the company's massive AI outlay deepened cash burn and its own executives acknowledged that 'AI mode' has hurt traditional search, even as Microsoft posted record quarterly revenue of $92.3 billion and disclosed for the first time that Azure brought in $33.2 billion and that it earned $10 billion from OpenAI commercial arrangements.

stories.headline: Anthropic pushes ahead with IPO rollout, launching new enterprise spend-tracking tools
stories.summary: Days after filing its S-1 showing $16.3 billion in first-half revenue and a $693 million operating loss, Anthropic launched reporting tools letting enterprise customers see what their Claude token spending is buying them, as it races toward a Nasdaq listing under the ticker ANT. Anthropic itself announced it is also expanding into biotech, partnering with Bristol Myers Squibb and other drugmakers to accelerate drug development with Claude.

stories.headline: Google rushes out Gemini 4 Carbon just two weeks after its last flagship model
stories.summary: Google DeepMind released Gemini 4 Carbon only two weeks after Gemini 4 Argon, with the new model topping the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index at 59 points, though access remains limited and The Register noted it's arriving at aggressive pricing just ahead of Anthropic's IPO.

stories.headline: Hacker steals personnel records of 40,000+ DHS, CBP and ICE employees
stories.summary: A hacker obtained and published online personally identifiable information belonging to more than 40,000 Homeland Security staffers, including CBP and ICE agents, exposing names, job titles, phone numbers and office locations.

stories.headline: Apple's touchscreen MacBook Pro pushes laptop pricing to new heights
stories.summary: Apple's newly launched touchscreen MacBook Pro can cost around $14,549 fully loaded, with Ars Technica's hands-on noting the OLED display looks great but the machine isn't as radically different from its predecessor as expected.

stories.headline: Chinese AI labs leaned on OpenAI model distillation despite Anthropic's crackdown
stories.summary: The Information reports that DeepSeek and Moonshot AI heavily relied on distillation from OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra to train models including Kimi K3.1 Pro and V4.1-Flash, even after Anthropic moved to crack down on such distillation attacks.

stories.headline: Senators demand Meta explain privacy failures in its smart glasses
stories.summary: Following a 404 Media investigation, Senators Ron Wyden and Edward Markey sent Meta a letter stating that its smart glasses have increasingly been implicated in disturbing invasions of users' and bystanders' privacy.

stories.headline: AI data center boom strains Arizona's water supply
stories.summary: A Verge feature examines how the rapid buildout of chip and data center infrastructure in the Arizona desert is placing new pressure on the region's water resources.

Tech & AI.gaps: Platformer, MIT Technology Review, IEEE Spectrum, Rest of World, OpenAI, and Google DeepMind had no major breaking news directly tied to the past 24-48 hours beyond items already reflected above; Wired's recent posts were largely reviews/lifestyle content outside this story set.

Energy.overview: Energy and climate outlets are dominated by two intertwined storylines: the fate of the Senate's bipartisan permitting reform bill and whether the Trump administration is really easing up on clean-energy project approvals, and the strain the AI/data-center boom is putting on power markets, grid planning and now Wall Street sentiment toward clean energy stocks. Oil markets are also in focus as prices swing on tentative US-Iran diplomacy, while Carbon Brief highlights the UK's new energy-bill push and China's outsized clean-tech export footprint.

stories.headline: Trump Hasn't Been Advancing New Wind Farms During Permitting Talks
stories.summary: Heatmap reports that of the wind projects the Trump administration claims to have "advanced" during bipartisan permitting negotiations, all are merely repowerings of existing turbines rather than new utility-scale developments, according to the American Clean Power Association. Separately, Heatmap's Shift Key podcast notes that while climate advocates remain split on the Senate's permitting bill, most agree its electricity and transmission provisions are stronger than expected.

stories.headline: Oil Slides as Traders Weigh Signs of Tentative Iran Diplomacy
stories.summary: Oil prices eased as markets assessed fresh diplomatic overtures aimed at averting a resumption of US strikes on Iran, reversing some of the risk premium built into crude. WSJ separately reported that Vice President JD Vance sent a letter to Iran's Supreme National Security Council in an effort to revive talks, even as pump prices remain stubbornly high.

stories.headline: The AI Stock Selloff Hits Clean Energy
stories.summary: Latitude Media's Open Circuit podcast examines how a Wall Street pullback on AI-linked stocks is now spilling over into clean energy companies, as investor patience with the capital-intensive data-center buildout wanes.

stories.headline: DOE announces $10.1B in loans to Constellation, Alliant, for 3.7 GW
stories.summary: The Department of Energy is financing loan packages that could fund uprates at existing nuclear and gas generation facilities, with Energy Secretary Chris Wright calling it "commonsense" policy to add capacity amid surging demand.

stories.headline: UK budget 2026: Key climate and energy announcements
stories.summary: Carbon Brief details Chancellor John Healey's declared "new course on energy" in the UK budget, centered on keeping household bills down, alongside a companion Q&A explaining why UK energy bills have kept climbing in 2026 and what could bring them down.

stories.headline: China's clean-tech exports in 2026 to avoid as much CO2 as Brazil emits in a year
stories.summary: A Carbon Brief analysis finds China's 2026 exports of solar panels, batteries and EVs are on track to avoid emissions roughly equivalent to Brazil's annual carbon output, underscoring Beijing's outsized role in global decarbonization.

stories.headline: BNEF ups US energy storage deployment forecast by 30%
stories.summary: BloombergNEF raised its US battery storage outlook after hyperscalers' interest in on-site and nearby storage converted into firm orders this year, reflecting how data-center power needs are reshaping grid investment.

stories.headline: CenterPoint expands 10-year capital plan by $4B to handle load growth
stories.summary: The Houston utility is accelerating investment to nearly $71 billion through 2035 to meet growing customer demand, the latest example of utilities scaling up capital plans in response to electrification and data-center load growth.

Energy.gaps: E&E News appears to have stopped publishing new content on its public site (migrated to POLITICO Pro U.S. Intelligence) and had no fresh items in the last 48 hours; Argus Media could not be found via search; FT, WSJ, NYT, Reuters and The Economist block web search, so only items present in the provided feed could be used for them, and only WSJ/FT/Bloomberg had relevant feed items.

China.description: China politics, economy and business coverage.
China.overview: The dominant story across Hong Kong and global outlets is the government's apology and reshuffle following the long-awaited investigation into the deadly Tai Po high-rise fire, while mainland-focused outlets are tracking the close of the Communist Party's Fifth Plenum, a widening anti-corruption drive in state finance, and continued debate over China's demographic decline and uneven stock-market recovery. Cross-strait tension also flared after Pakistan briefly barred Taiwanese airlines from its airspace citing Beijing's 'one-China' policy.

stories.headline: Hong Kong leader apologizes, housing chief resigns after Tai Po fire report
stories.summary: Chief Executive John Lee and top officials bowed in apology nearly a year after the Wang Fuk Court blaze killed 168 people, announcing that Housing Secretary Winnie Ho would step down even as Lee defended the government's handling of the disaster; a separate report attributed the fire to a lit cigarette igniting combustible materials compounded by human failings.

stories.headline: China elevates military anti-graft chief Zhang Shengmin to Politburo
stories.summary: Beijing promoted General Zhang Shengmin, the figure leading the recent purge of top PLA officers, to the Communist Party's Politburo, a move that comes as the party's Fifth Plenum wraps up its discipline-focused session.

stories.headline: Pakistan briefly bars Taiwanese airlines, citing China's 'one-China' policy
stories.summary: Taiwan said Pakistan abruptly closed its airspace to China Airlines and EVA Air flights, with Islamabad's defense minister invoking a "one-China" policy before reversing the decision; Taipei's cabinet said it "deeply regret[s]" what it called politicization and weaponization of airspace, and suspects Beijing's involvement.

stories.headline: China's population posts largest annual drop since 2022
stories.summary: China's population fell by 3.39 million in 2025 to 1.405 billion, the fourth straight annual decline and the steepest since 2022, with researchers projecting the losses will accelerate in coming decades.

stories.headline: China's trade surplus nears record as Beijing defends its export reliance
stories.summary: China's merchandise trade surplus reached nearly $940 billion in the first nine months of 2026, up 7.8% year-on-year, putting the country on track for another annual record even as the IMF and Western governments cite the imbalance as evidence of weak domestic demand and unfair competition.

stories.headline: Billions flow into China ETFs as stock market struggles to find footing
stories.summary: Chinese broad-based equity ETFs tracking the CSI 300 and tech indexes drew massive inflows after a sharp correction, with analysts pointing to concentrated institutional buying reminiscent of past state-linked support, even as it remains unclear whether the move signals a sustained recovery.

stories.headline: Beijing policy bank risk executive detained amid insider-trading probe
stories.summary: A senior China Development Bank risk-management executive who had been seconded to a Beijing district government post was detained by police in mid-October over a suspected insider-trading case, the latest in an anti-corruption campaign that has already ensnared 30-40 CDB executives including a former chairman.

stories.headline: Beijing moves to suppress coverage of labor unrest
stories.summary: China Media Project reports that a recent wave of arrests tied to labor issues has been accompanied by the shuttering of dedicated labor-news outlets and social media accounts, suggesting leadership is working to keep worker grievances out of public view.

China.gaps: No recent (last 24-48h) items could be found for Sixth Tone, Global Times, China Daily, Xinhua, CGTN, or Yicai Global; Global Times search results returned only older (2025) Tai Po fire coverage, not current material.

Gulf & Middle East.overview: Coverage across Gulf and Israeli/Palestinian outlets is dominated by the aftermath of Israel's deadlocked election and ensuing coalition scramble, fresh escalation in the Strait of Hormuz with tankers reportedly hit by mines, and the widening UAE oil spill tied to the broader Iran-US conflict. Gulf business outlets are also tracking Saudi Arabia's economic resilience and wage reforms amid the regional war, while diplomatic signals (a Vance letter to Iran) are being watched closely by markets.

stories.headline: Israel's election ends in deadlock, coalition talks begin
stories.summary: With about 90% of votes counted, Netanyahu's bloc holds a narrow lead but neither he nor rival Gadi Eisenkot has a clear path to the 61 seats needed, triggering talks on a possible unity government, Arab-party kingmaker role, or a repeat election.

stories.headline: Iran's Revolutionary Guards say three tankers hit mines in Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Iran's IRGC says naval mines set two tankers ablaze and disabled a third as they tried to use a southern route Tehran considers illegal, part of a sharp rise in attacks on shipping through the strategic waterway this month.

stories.headline: UAE oil spill widens, forcing more beach closures across northern emirates
stories.summary: A tanker spill off Umm Al Quwain has shut beaches there and in Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah, with satellite imagery showing the slick spreading toward shore as clean-up crews work to contain it.

stories.headline: Oil prices slide as US and Iran signal fresh diplomatic contact
stories.summary: President Trump played down reports of a letter Vice President JD Vance sent to Iran's security council aimed at reviving talks, even as traders pushed oil prices lower on hopes the outreach could avert renewed US strikes.

stories.headline: Saudi oil exports hold near wartime highs despite attacks
stories.summary: Ship-tracking data show Saudi Arabia shipping roughly 6.5 million barrels a day so far in October, close to wartime peaks, even as Houthi and Iranian attacks on tankers and infrastructure continue.

stories.headline: Gaza deaths and West Bank raids continue amid ceasefire strains
stories.summary: Gaza's health ministry reported six Palestinians killed and dozens wounded in Israeli strikes over 24 hours, while separate Israeli raids in the West Bank saw 14 Palestinians detained amid settler attacks and home demolitions.

stories.headline: Saudi Arabia to raise minimum supported wage to SR6,000 by 2028
stories.summary: The Human Resources Development Fund will lift the minimum eligible wage under its Employment Support Program to SR5,000 in 2027 and SR6,000 in 2028, part of a push to boost Saudi private-sector hiring and Saudization.

stories.headline: Oracle expands AI data centres in UAE and Saudi Arabia
stories.summary: Oracle is adding new data centres in the UAE and Saudi Arabia as it races to meet surging regional demand for AI infrastructure.

Gulf & Middle East.gaps: No recent distinct coverage found from AGBI, Zawya, Arabian Business or Haaretz in this search window; these outlets may be covering the same top stories (Israel election, Hormuz tensions, oil spill) but no specific articles surfaced.

Africa.description: Africa politics, economy and business coverage.
Africa.overview: African outlets this period are dominated by geopolitics around the Russia-Africa summit in Moscow and fallout from the DRC conflict, alongside a wave of business and finance coverage including Pan-African bank rankings, a widening Ebola outbreak, and fintech consolidation at Lagos's Moonshot conference. Africa Confidential and African Business are also tracking South Africa's tense municipal election run-up and renewed investor interest in African mining and energy despite policy-risk warnings.

stories.headline: Putin courts African leaders at third Russia-Africa summit
stories.summary: At the summit's plenary session Vladimir Putin pitched Moscow as Africa's best partner and called for an end to Western dominance on the continent, while The Africa Report examined how Russian firms like Rosatom, Rusal and Nordgold keep expanding in Africa despite Western sanctions.

stories.headline: US sanctions Rwandan defence ministry over Congo rebel ties
stories.summary: Washington has sanctioned Rwanda's defence ministry in a bid to pressure Kigali to withdraw troops from eastern DRC and halt support for the M23 armed group.

stories.headline: Ebola funding gap widens as outbreak spreads beyond DRC
stories.summary: African health ministers were set to convene online on 28 October to coordinate a response to an Ebola epidemic that has spread out of Congo-Kinshasa into other West, Central and East African countries, with a Bundibugyo-strain vaccine still months away.

stories.headline: Inside Ecobank's boardroom power struggle
stories.summary: The last-minute cancellation of Ecobank's 26 October general meeting has reignited a corporate-governance crisis, with minority shareholders raising conflict-of-interest allegations against the pan-African lender's leadership.

stories.headline: Appian Capital targets $2bn for Africa but warns policy risk is pushing capital away
stories.summary: Appian Capital Advisory's CEO said the London-based mining private equity firm plans roughly $2 billion for Africa out of a global $5-7 billion deployment, but policy uncertainty in countries like Burkina Faso and Tanzania is diverting investment toward Latin America, even as it remains bullish on copper and rates Morocco, Namibia and Botswana as top-tier jurisdictions.

stories.headline: Zuma health scare clouds South Africa's municipal election coalition maths
stories.summary: Uncertainty over 84-year-old Jacob Zuma's health is adding risk to the 4 November local government elections, with his uMkhonto weSizwe Party riding Zulu nationalist sentiment that could reshape governance in South Africa's economic heartland.

stories.headline: Nigerian banks sink while South African lenders swim in Top 300 ranking
stories.summary: The Africa Report's Top 300 Finance Champions ranking found many pan-African banking groups' balance sheets inflated by currency swings, sovereign debt and recapitalisation, with tighter regulation and Sahel insecurity hitting Nigerian lenders harder than South African ones.

stories.headline: African fintechs push beyond payments toward banking, Moonshot executives say
stories.summary: At TechCabal's Moonshot conference in Lagos, Flutterwave's CEO argued African fintechs are moving into banking because payments alone are no longer enough, a theme echoed by Paystack's co-founder and by Grey's new Paycheck product launch targeting growth beyond three million users.

Africa.gaps: The Continent had no new stories within the last 48 hours beyond general site/archive pages; Reuters, AP, BBC, FT, NYT and WSJ were not checked via search (they block it) and no relevant feed items were supplied for them.

Media.overview: Media coverage across outlets is dominated by the fight over Meta's new AI-scraping terms for publishers, cable news ratings turmoil ahead of the U.S. midterms, and press-freedom clampdowns from Egypt to Washington. Hollywood trades are also tracking Skydance/CNN leadership uncertainty and awards-season content, while ad-industry outlets flag weakening revenue at Condé Nast and WPP's tentative stabilization.

stories.headline: Fox News ratings sink sharply ahead of midterms while CNN and MS NOW gain
stories.summary: Status reported Nielsen data showing Fox News on track for a steep year-over-year ratings decline just before the midterms, while CNN and MS NOW post gains; Deadline and Variety confirmed the figures, with Fox primetime viewership down roughly 27-28% even as it remains cable's most-watched news outlet.

stories.headline: Publishers escalate fight over Meta's new AI terms of service
stories.summary: Pressure on Meta is mounting from multiple directions: Nieman Lab reports Meta has pledged a full consultation with publishers before finalizing its controversial new terms, while Senator Adam Schiff sent a letter calling the terms a 'gross abuse of Meta's power,' and Press Gazette reports Norwegian outlets including Schibsted and NRK won a court victory seeking to block the terms.

stories.headline: News outlets press lawsuit against Trump administration over White House press pool access
stories.summary: CNN, MS NOW and Politico filed an updated lawsuit arguing they were improperly denied access to White House reporting pools, a dispute Puck's media column has also been tracking as part of what it called the administration's 'largely illegal ban' on the three outlets.

stories.headline: Egypt shuts down independent outlet Mada Masr and fines its editor
stories.summary: Egyptian authorities fined prominent editor Lina Attalah and shut the independent news outlet Mada Masr after a Cairo court convicted her of managing an unlicensed website, in what the Guardian frames as an escalating press-freedom clampdown.

stories.headline: Hunterbrook accuses NYT of lifting its chemical-plant investigation without credit
stories.summary: Puck's Dylan Byers reports that newsco-hedge fund hybrid Hunterbrook says a Times investigation into chemical plants bore a striking resemblance to its own earlier reporting; the Times' trust editor denied the work was based on Hunterbrook's reporting but agreed to add a credit line deep in the story.

stories.headline: BBC journalists to vote on strike over threatened compulsory redundancies
stories.summary: Press Gazette reports BBC journalists will vote on strike action after the broadcaster said it could not guarantee avoiding compulsory redundancies.

stories.headline: Skydance leadership uncertainty lingers as Mark Thompson's CNN contract talks stall
stories.summary: Puck reports that as Skydance prepares a company-wide buyout and layoff program, questions remain over who will ultimately lead CNN, with CBS alumni including Dan Rather renewing criticism of Bari Weiss and David Ellison even as Weiss pushed back by asking critics to judge the network 'by the journalism.'

stories.headline: Condé Nast's ad business forecast to miss targets by over $35 million as it searches for a new CEO
stories.summary: Adweek reports Condé Nast insiders blame a lack of clear commercial strategy and an exodus of senior sales talent for a projected Q4 ad shortfall, coming as the publisher searches for new leadership.

Media.gaps: WSJ and FT had no media-industry items in the feed and were not found via search; Status and Puck items were sourced from direct searches rather than feed.
